new_public_evidence.source: Uesato et al., Rigorous Agent Evaluation: An Adversarial Approach to Uncover Catastrophic Failures
new_public_evidence.result: Continuation-trained adversarial value/failure predictors reduce median failure-search samples 198x on simulated Driving and 3100x on Humanoid; 95%-confidence 3-approximate risk estimation uses 14x/34x fewer episodes than vanilla Monte Carlo. Probability estimation uses importance correction, and the paper documents coverage/fallback limitations.

new_public_evidence.source: Liu et al., Adaptive Multilevel Twisted Sequential Monte Carlo for Rare Events Estimation in Language Models
new_public_evidence.result: Ablations show finite-budget multilevel behavior is non-monotone: at toxic-story gamma*=7, error improves strongly with samples per level but rho changes do not monotonically improve error. The appendix explicitly warns that higher hit rate/ESS can coexist with worse probability error on less-rare targets.

derived_results.claim: Use historical weaker/noisier agent trajectories as continuation data to learn a failure-probability predictor, then concentrate evaluation by that predictor while retaining an importance-corrected risk estimator and coverage fallback. External agent evidence gives large sample/wall-clock gains over random evaluation.

Keep rare-event score/failure predictor, sampling proposal/adversary and probability estimator as separate auditable objects. Hit rate, discovery success and ESS diagnose search/proposal quality but are not the target probability estimate.
Treat multilevel retained fraction and samples per level as a joint budget-control problem; the recent LLM ablation rejects a monotone 'more levels/higher hit rate means more accurate' heuristic.

negative_or_scope_evidence: Driving/Humanoid are simulated RL agents, not modern LLM tool agents.
Failure predictors can miss unknown failure regions; proposal coverage and importance-weight tails need explicit monitoring/fallback.
Continuation data from weaker agents can be misleading if the final system introduces qualitatively new failure modes.
The 2026 LLM paper is a recent arXiv v1 and its rho/sample ablations are task-specific.
